I've been disappointed by similar products before, so quality really matters to me.

I hear you. When you’ve been let down before, it feels risky to hit “buy” again, especially with plants that you’re investing time and care into.

Quality is a big focus for us at Heirloom. A few things that often matter to people who’ve had bad experiences elsewhere:

We grow our own roses at our nurseries in Oregon; we don’t buy them in from third-party growers.
All of our roses are own-root in 1-gallon containers (not grafted, not bare root), which makes them longer-lived and more resilient over time.
Every plant is checked for health before it ships, and we defoliate roses so they travel better and focus on establishing once you plant them.
Roses are covered by a one-year guarantee, perennials by a 90-day guarantee, and bulbs by a failure-to-bloom guarantee.

I’d really like to help you get something that will feel like a win, not another disappointment.

Can you tell me:

Are you shopping for a rose, a different perennial, or bulbs?
Your ZIP code or hardiness zone?
What you care about most: fragrance, lots of blooms, low maintenance, disease resistance, specific colors, or something else?

Once I know that, I can suggest options that are both high quality and well-matched to your garden so you’re set up for success.
